name: sgs/gallery
title: SGS Image Gallery
description: Image gallery with grid, masonry, and carousel layouts plus lightbox viewing. supports.filter.duotone (T3.5, D402 ADOPT) targets each .sgs-gallery__img via the selectors.filter.duotone map — WP core renders duotone as a generated class + <style> tag, not an inline style attribute, so no render.php changes are needed.

sgs._comment_mediaElements: Rule 37-media-no-handroll fix (D-pending). Grid-thumbnail object-fit now routes through the shared media-element atom layer instead of a style.css literal. NOT a new client control: prefix 'sgs' resolves (sgs_media_element_attr) to the SAME 'sgsObjectFit' attribute the legacy universal image-controls extension (imageControls/imageControlsExplicit above) already injects and already exposes an 'Object Fit' dropdown for in the inspector — adding a second ObjectFitField here would give the client two controls for one property. render.php reads that existing value through SGS_Media_Element::style() and marks the grid with the atom's scope class; style.css no longer hardcodes object-fit on .sgs-gallery__img, relying on assets/css/media-atoms/object-fit.css's cover fallback (identical default). The lightbox full-view image is deliberately NOT part of this — it keeps its own hardcoded object-fit:contain (style.css), which is not client-controllable.

fx._comment_providesNatively: Spec 38 FR-38-13 / §7. This block owns drag-to-scroll through its OWN inspector toggle, which targets the DESCENDANT element that actually scrolls. The generic 'Scroll & effects' picker stamps data-sgs-fx onto the block ROOT, which is not the scroller here — so offering `draggable` there too would give the client TWO controls for ONE capability, and the picker's one would silently do nothing. Declaring it here removes the dud picker entry via generate-fx-qualifying-blocks.py without removing the capability, exactly as sgs/responsive-logo does for `draw`. Ruled 2026-07-31 after the roster derivation surfaced it on five blocks at once (gallery had it latently already). NOTE sgs/timeline deliberately does NOT carry this: its scroller IS the block root, so the picker lands correctly there.

grid.label: Grid
grid._layer_note: Block root and grid/carousel-track definition combined. layer_detect.py's MF-3 guard makes the root OUTER regardless of its own display:grid.
grid._note: No `display`/`order`/`overflow` attribute exists on this block — honest GAPs.
grid._note_animation: FR-35-6 — the scroll-reveal preset (sgsAnimation/sgsAnimationDuration/sgsAnimationEasing) + per-image staggerDelay resolve via explicit attrMap (no `prefix` declared, per ROLLOUT REQUIREMENT 1). anim:parallax/anim:trigger are honest gaps — no bgParallax/scroll-trigger attributes on this block.

image.label: Image
image._note: Governed by the universal image-controls extension (supports.sgs.imageControls) plus aspectRatio/effectHover/imageZoomHover, not the Text/Fill/Layout style clusters. `grayscaleHover` claimed via `states.hover.attrMap` (css:filter) 2026-08-28 — real CSS behind a class toggle, invisible to the classifier's usual attrMap-scan shape until declared explicitly here.

caption.label: Caption
caption._note: Only shown when showCaptions is true. css:color resolves via the default convention (captionColour). Gradient siblings added 2026-09-04: captionBgColourGradient paints a hand-built ::after layer (NOT sgs_block_background_layer_css() — .sgs-gallery__caption is already position:absolute, which that helper would silently override), freeing the element's own background-image for captionColourGradient's background-clip:text.
caption._note_colour: captionColour declared 2026-09-05: render.php:118 reads it and it paints the caption's text colour. It previously had css_property='color' in the DB with no authored source (a rogue seed that would vanish on the next reseed); declaring it here makes that value legitimate and durable.

item.label: Grid item
item._note: The per-image grid cell (.sgs-gallery__item, render.php ~line 455/506) - distinct from the image element (the itself) and img-wrap below. aspectRatio is claimed via explicit attrMap rather than declaring 'layout' in clusters: a first draft used clusters:["layout"], which reached the SAME bare (no-prefix) cluster members as the 'grid' element (also bare-prefix) and produced a CONTESTED finding on aspectRatio itself, plus risked colliding on other bare layout members this block happens to declare. clusters:[] + explicit attrMap avoids the collision entirely while still claiming aspectRatio cleanly (placement-reach's attrMap/member-owner path is independent of the clusters list). shadowHover is a HOVER-ONLY box-shadow with no resting-state twin (no base 'shadow' attribute exists on this block) - deliberately left unclustered rather than declared as a states.hover entry, which would create a NEW state-without-base finding (the framework's baseline currently accepts exactly one such case, sgs/post-grid, and gates against any rise). prefix:"" additionally opts this element out of orphan-candidate scanning so shadowHover is reported honestly as an accepted gap. Found live 2026-08-15: DB tagged 2 attrs css_element='item', undeclared until now.

img-wrap.label: Image wrapper
img-wrap._note: The wrapper around the rendered inside each grid item (.sgs-gallery__img-wrap, render.php ~line 467/508) - carries the hover-reveal overlay. overlayColourHover is HOVER-ONLY (no resting overlayColour attribute exists on this block) so it is deliberately left unclustered rather than declared via states.hover, which would manufacture a new state-without-base finding against the D542-gated baseline (currently exactly 1, sgs/post-grid). prefix:"" opts this element out of orphan-candidate scanning so the attribute is reported honestly as a gap, not force-claimed. Found live 2026-08-15: DB tagged 1 attr css_element='img-wrap', undeclared until now.
img-wrap._note_hover: overlayColourHover declared 2026-09-05: render.php:145 states it paints an EXISTING `.sgs-gallery__img-wrap::after` overlay on hover. Was a rogue seed (css_property in the DB, declared nowhere).

_key._note: Client-generated stable identity (src/utils/generateItemKey.js), not a client-visible field. Scopes this item's own object-fit/focal-point CSS so a crop value survives reorder/add/remove instead of following array index or the WP attachment id (which collides the moment the same image is used twice). Spec 35 Part 4.

gap._comment: Was the bare number "16". MEASURED before and after: this default renders 16px either way, so the change is behaviour-preserving — it only makes the value explicit. (An earlier draft of this comment claimed the default had been silently dead because spacing slug 16 does not exist in theme.json. That was WRONG: gallery's own render.php already appended `px` to a bare number before handing it on, so "16" always meant 16px here. The live capture showed 16px on both builds and corrected the claim.) Notably this block had already implemented the bare-number-means-px convention locally, which is now the framework-wide rule. Bean-ruled 2026-08-10.

borderColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the border with a masked ring instead of a flat colour (D636 border-gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over borderColour.
